messages:
incident-bot: Paging devon_oncall: High error rate and increased tail latency observed on kv-prefix service in us-west-2. Alert: kv.prefix.evictions > 5k/min and p99 generation latency spiking. Auto-mitigation not applied.

devon_oncall: ack — I'm on it. any customer-facing impact detected?

sara_ops: seeing 502s for a handful of tenants, mostly heavy prompt workloads with long contexts. Correlation with prefix cache misses.

ravi_sre: logs show repeated cache bypass for prefixes A12* and C9* — looks like correctness bypass is firing due to stale checksum mismatches. That bypass is causing direct backend reads and pushing overall throughput to saturation.

maria_prodeng: is this the new prefix checksum change we rolled last week?

ravi_sre: seems related. A small fraction of prefixes started reporting checksum delta after the minor serialization change. Should be correctness-first; but it's now high-cardinality so it's amplifying load.

sara_ops: current cluster CPU on inference nodes at 92%. Eviction rates are causing higher disk IO.

devon_oncall: steps: 1) apply soft rate-limit to non-critical tenants 2) temporarily disable prefetch/prefetcher for prefix-level reads 3) enable per-prefix short-circuit for known good prefixes 4) prepare customer comms. Anyone object?

jenna_support: can we target the rate-limits to specific tenants? We need to avoid broad impact to enterprise SLAs.

eugene_infra: yes, we can apply a routing policy to move traffic for identified high-volume tenants to the degraded path with 30% token rate-limit. Will take ~2 minutes to deploy.

ravi_sre: also recommend toggling the "checksum-strict-bypass" flag to allow a grace window — effectively let slightly-mismatched prefixes go through the cache for 10 minutes while we patch. This reduces bypass freq but accepts small correctness risk. Need sign-off.

maria_prodeng: correctness tradeoff is sensitive. Which tenants would be affected? Any enterprise customers with legal requirements?

devon_oncall: list of affected tenants attached in logs: tenant-psi, tenant-gamma, tenant-320. None on the compliance list but tenant-psi is paying high volume. We should protect them from mass throttling.

jenna_support: recommend we not enable grace for tenant-psi. We can instead route them to dedicated fallback instances with higher capacity if needed.

sara_ops: ok. plan: 1) apply targeted rate-limit 2) disable prefetch globally 3) enable grace window for non-enterprise tenants 4) move tenant-psi to fallback pool. I'll run the commands.

devon_oncall: do it. Post exact commands you run.

sara_ops: running: ```
# disable prefetch
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/flags" -d '{"flag":"prefetch.enabled","value":false}'
# apply routing rule for high-volume tenants
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/routing" -d '{"rule":"match tenant in [\"tenant-alpha\",\"tenant-gamma\"] -> route:degraded,rate_limit:0.3"}'
```

incident-bot: Deploy triggered: flag-toggle/8372 by sara_ops. CI checks passed.

ravi_sre: I'm toggling checksum-strict-bypass grace for non-enterprise suffixes: ```
PATCH /api/config/cache
{ "checksum_grace_window_sec": 600, "exempt_tenants": ["tenant-psi","tenant-enterprise-1"] }
```

maria_prodeng: note in product: we need an eval to ensure no correctness regressions. Run quick spot-check for top 20 prefixes before enabling.

ravi_sre: running spot-check script now. snippet: ```
for p in $(cat top20_prefixes); do curl -s "https://cache-service/validate?p=$p" >> results; done
```

sara_ops: results look ok for 18/20; two prefixes had minor output diffs but not catastrophic. Given load impact, I'm comfortable with the grace window if we exempt tenant-psi.

devon_oncall: agree. Proceed with grace window + tenant-psi fallback move + targeted rate caps. Keep me updated in 5 minutes.

10:04 devon_oncall: status?

10:05 sara_ops: prefetch disabled across both us-west clusters. Routing rule applied for tenant-alpha/tenant-gamma. Checksum grace window set (600s) with tenant exemptions. CPU usage reduced to 76% on impacted nodes. Eviction rate down 70%.

10:06 incident-bot: Note: Degraded routing for tenant-alpha and tenant-gamma is active.

jenna_support: drafting customer note for affected tenants (non-enterprise) — recommending temporary performance degradation for correctness. Will flag enterprise customers separately.

eugene_infra: prepared fallback pool for tenant-psi; diverting traffic now. ```
# move tenant-psi to fallback
POST /control-plane/move-tenant {"tenant":"tenant-psi","pool":"fallback-highcap"}
```

10:10 ravi_sre: backend latency p50/p99 both improved; p99 back to near baseline. Bypass counts decreased significantly.

devon_oncall: good. Next actions: 1) full post-incident ticket 2) roll a small patch to fix checksum serialization asap 3) schedule a follow-up meeting with product and storage team 4) customer outreach for any tenants we throttled. Who owns each?

maria_prodeng: I'll own the product-side postmortem + eval.

jenna_support: support will send interim customer notes, and prepare one-to-one comms for any enterprise we touched.

ravi_sre: infra/storage will own the checksum patch — aiming for a low-risk rollback and a compatibility shim. ETA 4 hours.

devon_oncall: I'll write the incident summary and assign action items. We'll keep this thread for follow-ups; reopen if anything regresses.

sara_ops: leaving a note: to avoid this class of incidents, propose: a) circuit-breaker for checksum bypass amplification b) soft-prefetch throttles c) flagged rollout gate for serialization changes.

devon_oncall: agreed. Adding to postmortem checklist.

maria_prodeng: thanks team. Jenna — ping me when customer notes are out.

jenna_support: will send initial notes in 15.

incident-bot: Incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned severity: Sev2.

devon_oncall: wrapping up: all mitigations still green, leaving monitoring for 2h. If any fallback toggles change, update thread. :white_check_mark:
